title: Labelling a section of the forebrain
body: During a model-making activity, students examined a labelled section of the human forebrain and noted three regions. Region X is the outer layer of cells covering each cerebral hemisphere; it is thrown into prominent folds, looks greyish because many neuron cell bodies are concentrated there, and contains motor areas, sensory areas and large association areas responsible for memory and communication. Region Y forms the inner part of each hemisphere; it is made of fibre tracts covered with myelin sheath and has an opaque appearance. Region Z is a structure around which the cerebrum wraps; the students' teacher described it as a major coordinating centre for sensory and motor signalling, with another important part of the brain lying at its base.
